sources.title: John Tosh, “Reflection: Masculinities and history for the present” (2023).
sources.citation: John Tosh, “Reflection: Masculinities and history for the present,” in Matt Houlbrook, Katie Jones and Ben Mechen, eds., Men and masculinities in modern Britain: A history for the present (Manchester University Press, 2023), 178–188, DOI 10.7765/9781526174703.00014.

verification.note: Fresh selected primary chapter pp.178–186 read in UCL deposited open-access publisher PDF; title/copyright pages establish 2023 despite a repository/search display of January 2024. Principal locators pp.178,179–181,185–186 nn.1–3,11,14. The PDF holds the whole collection, but the collection is not claimed read in full. Foucault is cited through Alan Sheridan’s translation (Vintage 1995), pp.30–31; that edition itself is unread. Manful Assertions is a 1991 volume co-edited with Michael Roper; Family Fortunes belongs jointly to Davidoff and Catherine Hall. Filename reflection2023.pdf is the complete deposited volume; reflection2023.txt its pdftotext extraction.

sources.title: Lucy Delap and John Tosh, in conversation, “Conclusion: Histories, historians, and the politics of masculinity” (2023).
sources.citation: Lucy Delap and John Tosh, in conversation, “Conclusion: Histories, historians, and the politics of masculinity,” in Houlbrook, Jones and Mechen, eds., Men and masculinities in modern Britain (Manchester University Press, 2023), 299–313, DOI 10.7765/9781526174703.00024.

verification.note: Selected pp.299–304 freshly read in deposited publisher PDF. Edited conversation with the three editors took place 19 December 2020 and was published in 2023. Speakers are kept distinct: Tosh’s acknowledgment and self-qualification pp.301–302, Delap’s prompts and reading pp.300–301,303 are not silently assigned to Tosh. The complete conversation and collection are not claimed read.

hc177_tosh_article.note: Fresh check of primary opening p.179 in public Paperzz OCR, browser receipt raw/tosh1994-browser-receipt.json, browser lines34–51, establishes Tosh’s explicit use of Natalie Zemon Davis’s 1975 intervention to justify studying men as part of the whole gender power system. OCR remains uncollated; paraphrase only. The original Davis text is not freshly read. Earlier source scope and its pp.183–188 interpretation remain intact; a direct local Paperzz request returned a challenge rather than the OCR body.
